title: Observation of the electronic Pomeranchuk effect in generalized Wigner crystals of twisted MoS$_2$
authors: Xinjie Fang, Linfeng Wu, Naitian Liu, Le Zhang, Wenqiang Zhou, Jing Ding, Zhangyuan Chen, Hanxiao Xiang, Yue Xiao, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Shuigang Xu
abstract: Moire superlattices in transition metal dichalcogenides provide a highly tunable platform for exploring strongly correlated electronic phases, such as generalized Wigner crystals. While these crystalline states typically melt with increasing thermal fluctuations, an electronic analogue of the Pomeranchuk effect can stabilize the localized solid phase at elevated temperature through isospin entropy. Here, we report the observation of an electronic Pomeranchuk effect at the fractional filling factors of $ν= 1/3$ and $ν= 1/4$ in AB-stacked twisted bilayer MoS$_2$ with twist angles of 4.1$^\circ$ and 3.9$^\circ$, respectively. At ultra-low temperature, the system exhibits a highly conducting, itinerant behavior at these fractional fillings, characteristic of a compressible Fermi-liquid ground state. Upon heating, the system exhibits a counterintuitive increase in the longitudinal resistivity, signaling an isospin-entropy-driven transition into a localized generalized Wigner crystal state. Our findings highlight the unique capacity of flat bands in twisted bilayer MoS$_2$ for stabilizing highly degenerate magnetic configurations, offering new insights into the thermodynamic phase diagrams of low-dimensional correlated systems.
summary: This experimental work reports the observation of the electronic Pomeranchuk effect in twisted bilayer MoS2 moiré superlattices at fractional fillings. The system transitions from a conducting Fermi liquid at low temperatures to a localized Wigner crystal upon heating, a transition driven by the entropy associated with degenerate isospin degrees of freedom. This highlights moiré heterostructures as a key platform for studying entropy-driven correlated electronic phase transitions.
main_problem: The study aims to observe the electronic Pomeranchuk effect, where increasing temperature drives a transition from an itinerant Fermi liquid to a localized Wigner crystal state, stabilized by isospin entropy.
main_result:
The authors report observing this entropy-driven transition at fractional fillings ($
u=1/3$ and $
u=1/4$) in twisted bilayer MoS2, characterized by an anomalous increase in longitudinal resistivity upon heating.
method: The research utilizes temperature-dependent and magneto-transport measurements (e.g., Rxx, SdH oscillations) on high-quality twisted bilayer MoS2 devices.
model_or_system: The platform is AB-stacked twisted bilayer MoS2 moiré superlattices, which provide a tunable environment for strongly correlated phases like generalized Wigner crystals. The physics is governed by the competition between itinerant electron behavior and charge localization driven by long-range Coulomb interactions.
key_observables: Longitudinal resistivity (Rxx) vs. Temperature (T), Shubnikov-de Haas (SdH) oscillations, effective mass ($m^*$), and fractional resistance features.
important_parameters:
Fractional filling factors ($
u = 1/3$ and $
u = 1/4$), twist angles ($	heta = 4.1^\circ$ and $3.9^\circ$), and temperature dependence.
main_assumptions: The transition is modeled as an electronic analogue of the Pomeranchuk effect, where isospin entropy drives the system into a localized, charge-ordered state.
figures_summary: Figures show Rxx vs. T/V_tg, SdH oscillations revealing valley-dependent effective masses, and real-space electron configurations illustrating the GWC state.
paper_structure: The paper presents transport measurements across different filling factors and temperatures, analyzing the low-T Fermi-liquid behavior, the intermediate-T anomalous resistance increase (the Pomeranchuk signature), and the resulting charge-ordered GWC state.
why_interesting: The observation of an entropy-driven phase transition in a solid-state moiré system provides a concrete experimental realization of theoretical concepts regarding the interplay between entropy, correlation, and dimensionality, relevant to understanding exotic quantum states.
